eligibility_reason: Fundamentally strong credit (DSCR 3.84, Debt/EBITDA 0.92, zero bounces) but material cash reconciliation break of INR 61.4M between balance-sheet cash and bank-statement closing requires resolution before final sanction.

recommended_products.purpose: Augment existing working-capital limit to fund growing inventory and receivables cycle as revenue scales from INR 385.7M (FY25) to INR 486M (FY26)
recommended_products.amount_basis: Existing CC sanctioned INR 60M; utilisation 68.3% (INR 41M drawn). Gross WC gap = DSO 42d + Inventory 46d – DPO 38d = 50 net days. Monthly revenue FY26 = INR 486M/12 = INR 40.5M; 50-day gap × (INR 40.5M/30) = INR 67.5M required WC. Existing CC limit covers INR 60M; incremental need = INR 67.5M – INR 60M = INR 7.5M. Rounded up to INR 25M to provide headroom for 26% YoY revenue growth and seasonal peaks (peak monthly inflow INR 55.1M in May-25). Total revised CC limit = INR 85M. Cross-check: INR 85M / avg monthly inflow INR 47.2M = 1.80x (within 1–2x heuristic). Conservative sizing applied given unresolved cash reconciliation flag.
security: Primary: Hypothecation of current assets (inventory + trade receivables) — first charge, pari passu with HDFC Bank
Collateral: Extension of existing mortgage/charge on fixed assets (Net Block INR 59.8M) pari passu with HDFC Bank
Personal guarantees of all three promoter-directors: Rohan Deshpande, Anita Deshpande, Kunal Mehta
covenants: DSCR >= 1.25 tested semi-annually (current computed DSCR 3.84 provides ample headroom)
Debt/EBITDA <= 3.0x (current 0.92x; revised post-enhancement ~1.34x — well within limit)
CC utilisation reporting monthly; if utilisation < 20% for 3 consecutive months, limit reviewed downward
No additional secured borrowings without prior written consent
End-use certificate for each drawdown above INR 5M
No change of control without lender consent (promoter holding currently 92%)
Top-customer revenue concentration cap: single customer <= 25% of annual revenue (current top customer 19%)
conditions_precedent: MANDATORY — Cash reconciliation resolution: Borrower to provide auditor-certified reconciliation explaining INR 61.4M gap between balance-sheet cash (INR 37.5M) and bank-statement closing (INR 98.9M) as at 28-Mar-26; limit not to be released until resolved
MANDATORY — Missing sanction letter: Provide original/certified HDFC Bank Term Loan sanction letter (INR 50M facility) currently absent from dataroom

monitoring: Monthly stock and book-debt statement within 10 days of month-end
Quarterly management accounts (P&L, balance sheet) within 30 days of quarter-end
Annual audited financials within 120 days of fiscal year-end

Semi-annual DSCR and leverage covenant compliance certificate signed by CFO

serviceability_check: Existing annual interest on CC (INR 41M drawn × 9.4%) = INR 3,854,000
Existing annual interest on TL (INR 28.5M × 9.9%) = INR 2,821,500
Incremental interest on new INR 25M CC at 9.75% (assume 80% avg utilisation = INR 20M) = INR 1,950,000
Total interest post-enhancement = INR 3,854,000 + INR 2,821,500 + INR 1,950,000 = INR 8,625,500
Existing TL principal repayment = INR 1,080,000/month × 12 = INR 12,960,000
Total annual debt service post-enhancement = INR 8,625,500 + INR 12,960,000 = INR 21,585,500
Post-enhancement DSCR = INR 75,330,000 / INR 21,585,500 = 3.49x — comfortably above 1.25x threshold
Revised Debt/EBITDA = (INR 69,500,000 + INR 25,000,000) / INR 75,330,000 = 1.26x — well within 3.0x limit

recommended_products.purpose: Unlock cash tied in trade receivables to fund the 42-day DSO gap, providing a self-liquidating complement to the CC line during peak sales months
recommended_products.amount_basis: Eligible receivables (0–60 days) = INR 50,890,192 per snapshot. Top customer = 19% of total receivables = INR 10,625,425; apply concentration haircut: advance rate on top-customer portion = 70% (vs standard 80%), all others at 80%. Eligible ex-top-customer = INR 50,890,192 – INR 10,625,425 = INR 40,264,767 × 80% = INR 32,211,814. Top-customer eligible = INR 10,625,425 × 70% = INR 7,437,798. Gross eligible pool = INR 32,211,814 + INR 7,437,798 = INR 39,649,612. Exclude 61–90d (INR 3,355,397) and 90+ (INR 1,677,699) from pool entirely. Rounded limit = INR 35,600,000 (conservative floor below computed INR 39.6M given cash-reconciliation flag).

Recourse to Solara Foods Private Limited on non-payment by debtor
Personal guarantees of promoter-directors (Rohan Deshpande, Anita Deshpande, Kunal Mehta)

Single-debtor concentration cap: no debtor to exceed 25% of outstanding discounted pool

Annual renewal with fresh ageing and debtor KYC
serviceability_check: Invoice discounting is self-liquidating — repaid directly from debtor collections, not from operating cash flow
No incremental EMI or fixed debt-service obligation added to P&L
Implicit cost: discount fee on INR 35.6M at 8.25% p.a. for avg 42-day cycle = INR 35,600,000 × 8.25% × (42/365) = INR 338,400 per cycle
Annual implied cost (8–9 cycles/year) = ~INR 2,707,200 — absorbed within EBITDA of INR 75,330,000 with negligible impact
Post-facility DSCR (including CC enhancement from Product 1) remains 3.49x as computed above; invoice discounting does not alter this
CONCLUSION: Self-liquidating structure; no serviceability stress; DSCR unaffected

declined_products.reason: No capex requirement evidenced in snapshot; Net Block INR 59.8M is stable and no expansion plan cited. Adding a new TL would be mismatched to the working-capital use-of-funds profile and unnecessarily increase fixed debt-service obligations on a business whose primary gap is operating-cycle funding.

Company is profitable (PAT INR 44.5M FY26), cash-generative, and not pre-revenue or equity-runway dependent. Venture debt is structurally inappropriate and would be more expensive than conventional bank facilities.

While credit quality is strong, the unresolved INR 61.4M cash reconciliation break (data-quality flag: bs_cash_vs_bank_statement) and missing TL sanction letter preclude any unsecured exposure until discrepancies are resolved.

key_risks: Cash reconciliation break (INR 61.4M gap between BS cash INR 37.5M and bank closing INR 98.9M): mitigated by making auditor-certified reconciliation a hard condition precedent before any limit release — conservative sizing uses balance-sheet (lower) cash figure
Missing HDFC Bank TL sanction letter: mitigated by requiring original sanction letter as CP; pari-passu inter-creditor agreement ensures lender has equal security standing
Revenue concentration (top customer 19%): mitigated by 25% single-customer covenant and reduced 70% advance rate on top-customer receivables in invoice discounting pool

Pledging disclosure gap (promoter pledging = null): mitigated by CP requiring promoters to certify nil pledge or disclose; personal guarantees from all three promoter-directors provide recourse regardless

Seasonal cash-flow volatility (monthly inflows range INR 40.4M–55.1M, 37% swing): mitigated by revolving CC structure (not amortising TL) allowing drawdown/repayment flexibility; DSCR headroom of 3.49x absorbs trough months
Leverage creep as business scales: mitigated by Debt/EBITDA <= 3.0x covenant (current 1.26x post-enhancement) and no-additional-debt clause
rationale: Lead product is CC enhancement (not invoice discounting) because the 50-day net WC gap (DSO 42d + Inv 46d – DPO 38d) is a recurring operating-cycle need best served by a revolving cash-credit line.
CC limit sized to INR 85M total (INR 25M incremental): 50-day gap on FY26 monthly revenue INR 40.5M = INR 67.5M need; INR 85M covers peak-month inflow of INR 55.1M (May-25) with headroom.
Post-enhancement DSCR = 3.49x (EBITDA INR 75.33M / debt service INR 21.59M) — 2.8x above the 1.25x minimum; serviceability is not a constraint.

Invoice discounting (INR 35.6M) is additive, not lead: self-liquidating, zero EMI burden, unlocks the INR 50.9M eligible receivable pool at 78% blended advance rate with concentration haircut on top customer (19%).
Eligibility is 'conditional' not 'eligible': INR 61.4M cash reconciliation break (data-quality flag bs_cash_vs_bank_statement) is material and must be resolved before drawdown.
Conservative sizing applied throughout: balance-sheet cash INR 37.5M (lower figure) used, not bank-statement INR 98.9M; CC increment capped at INR 25M vs computed INR 39.6M invoice pool.
Zero cheque bounces in 12 months and DSCR 3.84x support pricing at MCLR+75bps for CC — tighter than a stressed credit but not the floor, reflecting the unresolved data flag.
Debt/EBITDA post-enhancement = 1.26x vs 3.0x covenant ceiling; leverage is not a binding constraint even after both facilities.
Promoter holding 92% with no disclosed pledging; personal guarantees from all three promoter-directors (Rohan, Anita, Kunal) required as standard governance control.
Missing TL sanction letter (data-quality flag: sanction_letter_partial_coverage) addressed as hard CP; pari-passu NOC from HDFC Bank required before security perfection.
Revenue growth 26% YoY (FY24→FY25) and 26% projected (FY25→FY26 INR 486M) supports the incremental limit; WC need scales proportionally with revenue.
No new term loan recommended: no capex evidence in snapshot; Net Block INR 59.8M stable; adding fixed amortisation would be product-use mismatch per selection heuristics.
